source_text: Et cum legeret, Augustinus episcopus dixit: Dicam caritati uestrae et commemorem rem dulcissimam et suauissimam, quam domino adiuuante sumus experti. cum ante ipsam collationem inter nos aliqui fratres de hac re colloqueremur, quia pro pace Christi episcopi debent esse aut debent non esse, quod nobis fatendum est, circumspicientes omnes fratres et coepiscopos nostros, non facile nobis occurrebant, qui hoc uellent suscipere et de hac humilitate domino sacrificare. dicebamus, ut fieri solet, \'ille potest, ille non potest, ille consentit hoc, ille non tolerat\', loquentes pro suspicionibus nostris magis, qui corda illorum uidere minime poteramus. quando autem uentum est ut hoc palam fieret, in concilio uniuersorum tam frequenti paene trecentorum episcoporum sic placuit omnibus, sic exarserunt omnes, ut parati essent episcopatum pro Christi unitate deponere et non perdere, sed deo tutius commendare. duo ibi uix inuenti sunt quibus displiceret, unus annosus senex, qui hoc etiam dicere liberius ausus est; alter uoluntatem suam tacito uultu significauit. sed posteaquam illum senem liberius hoc dicentem obruit omnium fraterna correptio, illo mutante sententiam uultum etiam ille mutauit. audite ergo, quibus modis etiam ipsa exhortatio facta est propter illum qui ait: qui se humiliat exaltabitur.
thought_title: The bishops' willingness to lay down their bishoprics for unity
orientation: Augustine interrupts Alypius's reading of the bishops' letter to tell the people what happened among the Catholic bishops before the Conference of Carthage.
pass_a_gloss: And while he was reading, Augustine the bishop said: I will tell your charity and I will call to mind a thing most sweet and most pleasant, which with the Lord helping we have experienced. When before that conference some brothers among us were discussing this matter among themselves, because for the peace of Christ bishops ought either to exist or ought not to exist, which must be confessed by us, looking around at all our brothers and fellow bishops, there did not easily occur to us those who would wish to take this up and to sacrifice to the Lord from this humility. We were saying, as is accustomed to happen, 'That one is able, that one is not able, that one consents to this, that one does not endure it', speaking rather from our suspicions, we who were least able to see their hearts. But when it came about that this would be done openly, in a council of all so crowded, of almost three hundred bishops, it so pleased all, all so burned, that they were ready to lay down the bishopric for the unity of Christ and not to lose it, but to commend it more safely to God. There two were scarcely found to whom it displeased, one an aged old man, who even dared to say this rather freely; the other indicated his will with a silent face. But after the brotherly correction of all overwhelmed that old man saying this rather freely, when he changed his opinion, that other one also changed his face. Hear therefore, in what ways even that exhortation itself was made on account of him who says: he who humbles himself will be exalted.

choices.english: to lay down the bishopric for the unity of Christ
choices.why: Keeps the literal force of deponere as laying down an office, and unitas as unity per the glossary.
rejected: to resign the episcopate for Christ's unity
to give up the bishopric for the unity of Christ

choices.term: non perdere, sed deo tutius commendare
choices.english: not to lose it, but to commend it more safely to God
choices.why: Preserves the contrast between losing and entrusting, and the comparative tutius.
rejected: not to lose it but to entrust it more securely to God
not to destroy it but to commit it more safely to God

choices.english: the brotherly correction of all overwhelmed
choices.why: Obruo has the force of overwhelming or burying under a mass; fraterna correptio is kept literal.
rejected: the fraternal rebuke of all crushed
the brotherly reproof of all silenced

choices.english: that other one also changed his face
choices.why: Keeps the literal uultum (face, expression) and the parallel with the old man changing his opinion.
rejected: the other also changed his expression
the other one also changed his countenance

choices.english: he who humbles himself will be exalted
choices.why: Literal rendering of the quoted saying, matching the Latin word order and passive future.
rejected: whoever humbles himself shall be exalted
the one who humbles himself will be lifted up

pass_b_english: While he was reading, Bishop Augustine said: I will tell your charity, and call to mind, something most sweet and most pleasant that we experienced with the Lord's help. Before the conference itself, when some of us brothers were talking together about this matter—because for the peace of Christ bishops ought either to exist or not to exist, which we must admit—as we looked around at all our brothers and fellow bishops, it was not easy for us to think of any who would want to take this on and sacrifice to the Lord by such humility. We said, as people do, 'That one can do it, that one cannot; that one agrees to it, that one will not tolerate it'—speaking more from our own suspicions, since we could not see their hearts at all. But when it came to the point that this was done openly, in a council of all together, so crowded with nearly three hundred bishops, it pleased everyone so much, and everyone burned with such zeal, that they were ready to lay down the bishopric for the unity of Christ—not to lose it, but to commend it more safely to God. There were barely two found there who were displeased: one an aged old man, who even dared to say this rather freely; the other indicated his wish by a silent face. But after the brotherly correction of all overwhelmed that old man who spoke so freely, and he changed his opinion, that other one also changed his face. Listen, then, to the ways in which the exhortation itself was made, for the sake of him who said: he who humbles himself will be exalted (Luke 14:11).

last_rejected.why: The quote matches Luke 14:11, but Augustine attributes it to 'him who said' without naming the speaker. The English adds '(Luke 14:11)' which is editorial, but more importantly, the source does not identify it as Luke. However, the work brief says modern citations should use standard English Bible names and numbering. This is actually correct per instructions.
last_rejected.fix: Keep as is per work brief.
last_rejected.ruling: Brief permits standard English Bible citations; Luke 14:11 correctly identifies qui se humiliat exaltabitur.
